stories.headline: Iran-linked attacks kill people in Saudi Arabia and threaten oil supply, pushing crude prices to a five-month high

sources.body:
The Houthis say they targeted the airport, Saudi Arabia’s defence ministry and an Aramco facility.

Saudi Arabia’s General Authority of Civil Aviation (GACA) says that the number of people killed in an attack on King Fahd International Airport in the eastern city of Dammam has risen to two – a Saudi national and an Indian resident.

The GACA said in a statement on Thursday that eight people were wounded in Wednesday’s attack and that operations at the airport had resumed and air traffic had returned to normal.

Separately on Wednesday, two people were killed after Saudi air defences intercepted a drone that was attempting to hit a facility at Saudi Aramco’s Shaybah oilfield, the Ministry of Energy said.

The attack are the latest in a series of assaults on Saudi infrastructure as conflict intensifies between the Houthis, an armed group also known as Ansar Allah (Arabic for Supporters of God), and the Saudi-backed internationally recognised Yemeni government.

Last week, the kingdom reported that a projectile strike on Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport on October 11 killed one person and injured 11. On October 10, the civil aviation authority reported that a separate attack on the same airport killed 12 people and injured more than 300.

The Houthis on Thursday claimed to have carried out numerous attacks on Saudi infrastructure over the last 48 hours, including targeting King Fahd International Airport. Other targets included Abha International Airport, the Saudi defence ministry in Riyadh and facilities belonging to Saudi ‌Aramco in Yanbu, according to the Houthis.

The Saudi-led coalition fighting the Iran-backed group, meanwhile, said four drones had been intercepted and destroyed in the regions of Riyadh and Medina.

Reuters and AFP cited sources as saying Saudi Aramco had ordered staff to evacuate from its headquarters in Dhahran, which was hit by a Houthi attack earlier in the month .

The reported evacuation came a day after the US State Department ordered diplomats and family members to depart from its missions in Saudi Arabia. There were also plans to withdraw family members from a number of other US missions in the region, US officials told Reuters.

The US embassy in Riyadh had issued a security alert on Wednesday about possible further attacks by the Houthis on Saudi Arabia.
sources.headline: Attack on Saudi Arabia’s King Fahd airport kills two people

Iran’s IRGC says it hit four vessels in the northern Gulf and three more struck mines near the strait of Hormuz

Shipping workers: how is the Middle East conflict affecting you?

Oil prices jumped to a five-month high on Thursday after ​attacks in Saudi Arabia and hits to tankers in the strait of Hormuz threatened further disruptions to the world’s crude supply.

Brent crude, the international benchmark for oil prices, rose by 3% to hit $112 a barrel for first time since 18 May.

Yemeni Houthis , who are aligned with Iran, hit several targets in Saudi Arabia on Wednesday, with two people killed and eight more wounded in a civilian airport in Dammam, and two people killed in a drone attack on a Saudi oilfield.

Elsewhere the Iranian Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said four vessels involved in “illegal” oil transfers in the northern ​Gulf were hit and caught fire after being tracked by its forces on Wednesday.

It said three more vessels collided with mines west of the strait of Hormuz, and warned the US that continued provocations could lead to a wider response against its regional bases.

The US has now ordered some diplomats and family members to leave their missions in Saudi Arabia, and it plans to withdraw family members from a number of other missions in the Middle East, according to Reuters, which also reported that Saudi Aramco has instructed staff to evacuate its headquarters in Dhahran and work remotely.

Concern is growing that conflict in the region could escalate further, almost eight months after Tehran’s effective block on the strait of Hormuz triggered what many feared would bring the greatest energy supply disruption in the history of the market. In the first weeks after the US-Israeli attacks on Iran , oil surged past $100 a barrel and market observers predicted prices of up to $150 a barrel as flows through Hormuz came to a halt.

Oil peaked at $126 a barrel in April during the conflict and fell back below $100 in late May and then to lows of $71 at the start of July amid hopes of a ceasefire in the region. The price began to climb again after the memorandum of understanding between the US and Iran fell apart and fresh hostilities broke out in the Gulf .

However, data from Kpler has shown that oil exports from the Persian Gulf have now risen above their prewar levels, partly because of an increase in oil pumped overland through pipelines to the Red Sea and Gulf of Oman.

Global stocks wobbled on Thursday amid expectations of higher inflation and borrowing costs. The Stoxx Europe 600, which tracks the biggest companies on the continent, fell by 1%, with the UK’s FTSE 100 down by 0.7%.

Get set for the working day – we'll point you to all the business news and analysis you need every morning

In Asia, Japan’s Nikkei 225 index dropped 2.7%, while the South Korean Kospi fell 3.5%. Hong Kong’s Hang Seng index shed 3%.

Shares in American Airlines dropped almost 4% in pre-market trading after the company warned that high fuel costs would push it into a loss this year.

stories.headline: Russia and Ukraine exchange major strikes as Moscow agrees to resume trilateral peace talks with Kyiv and Washington

sources.body: Ukraine and Russia exchanged drone and missile strikes on Thursday, killing seven people in Ukraine, according to authorities. Moscow said it had intercepted 630 Ukrainian drones targeting the Russian capital. The strikes came hours after US envoy Steve Witkoff met Vladimir Putin in St. Petersburg. Witkoff said Moscow was ready to resume trilateral talks with Kyiv and Washington.
sources.headline: Ukraine and Russia exchange strikes after US envoy visit to the Kremlin

sources.body: A US envoy met Putin in Saint Petersburg on Wednesday after the Kremlin agreed to resume peace talks with Ukraine and the United States. Details by FRANCE 24's correspondent Gulliver Cragg.
sources.headline: Russia agrees to resume trilateral peace talks on Ukraine war

sources.body:
Experts say Russia is trying to destroy energy infrastructure before winter and US ‘appeasement and flattery’ will not achieve peace

Russia has carried out a massive “demonstrative” attack on Ukraine, bombarding Kyiv with ballistic missiles just hours after Vladimir Putin said he had agreed to resume trilateral negotiations after talks with the US envoy Steve Witkoff.

Overnight, Moscow pounded the Ukrainian capital, killing at least two people and wounding 22, including four children. Targets included the southern bridge over the Dnipro River, civilian houses, energy infrastructure, an ambulance station, office buildings and a clinic.

The Ukrainian president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy , said three of the missiles carried cluster warheads. One struck the Pecherskyi district, damaging several historic structures, including a monastery.

“This is another extraordinarily revealing strike – revealing because it was no accident,” Zelenskyy said. “The choice of weapon was deliberate, the choice of target area was deliberate, and so was the intent to inflict as much loss and damage on civilians as possible.”

He said the strikes showed Russia was not serious about peace, adding: “Almost immediately after another round of talks, Russia launched a pointed attack. This means there has been no real change in its attitude toward everything that is happening.”

During negotiations on Wednesday in St Petersburg, Witkoff lavished praise on Putin, who was sitting across the table. “You talk so much about my president, President Trump, being a humanitarian. You are a humanitarian also, sir, and I salute that,” Witkoff said.

In a social media post after the strikes in the early hours of Thursday, Zelenskyy issued a sardonic reply: “Three waves of ballistic missiles have been launched at Kyiv by Russian ‘humanitarians’ since yesterday evening. They used 21 missiles.”

Zelenskyy said he was grateful to those among Ukraine’s western partners who saw “the situation for what it is” and “acknowledged the reality” that the Kremlin had little intention of stopping its war. He called for stronger air defences, Patriot interceptors that could bring down enemy missiles and more sanctions against Moscow.

Ukraine’s foreign minister, ⁠Andrii Sybiha, ⁠added that “appeasement, ⁠servility ​and flattery” ‌would ‌not ‌stop Russian aggression.

Downing Street said it did not recognise Witkoff’s description of Putin, pointing out that the Russian president had killed “thousands” of innocent Ukrainians, as well as his own frontline soldiers.

On Wednesday, the Kremlin foreign affairs adviser Yuri Ushakov said Putin had agreed “in principle” to resume three-way negotiations involving Russia, the US and Ukraine after 10 November, a week after the US midterm elections. In reality, Russia’s real intention is to destroy Ukraine’s energy infrastructure in the coming weeks, leaving millions in the dark and cold , officials in Kyiv believe.

According to Zelenskyy, the US has resumed intelligence warnings of Russian missile attacks. But the White House has so far not reversed the slowdown of Starshield, the military version of Elon Musk’s Starlink internet satellite system, leaving Ukraine unable to intercept enemy drones or carry out mid-range battlefield strikes.
sources.headline: Russia bombards Kyiv with missiles hours after agreeing to resume talks with Ukraine

stories.headline: Macron moves to ban non-union protests after violent unrest in France

sources.body:
French president will decide on concrete ‘next steps’ regarding demonstrations on Friday as part of tough security response to recent rioting

Angry lawyers and bewildered defendants: the fallout from fast-tracking French rioting cases

Emmanuel Macron has said “illegitimate” demonstrations will be banned over the coming days as France seeks to get a grip on civil unrest after some of its worst street violence in years erupted on the fringes of cost of living protests at the weekend.

Speaking after a ​meeting with intelligence chiefs and senior ministers, the French president said on Thursday that demonstrations organised by recognised groups would be allowed to go ahead, although their routes could be changed.

Protests requested by “individuals or groups with no legitimate authority” would be banned, Macron said. Requests by organisations such as trade unions would be “examined in accordance with the law” but may have to use alternative routes.

The measures were necessary to protect city centres, businesses and public buildings, he said, adding: “The rules are simple and I think they’re commonsense. The general recommendation is that there should be no demonstrations in the coming days.”

Macron blamed much of last weekend’s unrest and looting on rioters who came expressly to loot, but said the worst of the violence was due to “political and seditious acts by ultra far-left groups who aimed to bring down the Republic”.

“The priority is a return to calm,” he said, adding that he would chair a defence council meeting of key ministers on Friday to decide concrete “next steps” for new nationwide demonstrations called for Saturday and afterwards.

An initial police ban on a student protest planned in Paris for Thursday was later overturned by a court, but marches also scheduled for that day in Grenoble, Rouen, Le Havre and Toulon were halted.

The most pressing stories and debates for Europeans – from identity to economics to the environment

Authorities have already declared a ban on “all protests” on Saturday in the centre of the Lyon, France’s third-biggest city, where between 200 and 300 shops were ransacked and looted last weekend and the tourist office was set ablaze.

Authorities in Marseille, Nice and Toulon announced similar bans for Saturday. In Paris, a march planned for Saturday to be held in the east of the capital, starting at Place de la Bastille, was authorised but banned from heading into the city centre.

However, a separate march through the capital planned for Saturday by students and some members of the gilets jaunes (yellow vests) movement, whose protests over fuel prices rocked France in 2018 and 2019, would not be permitted, authorities in the capital said.

France’s main student union, UNEF, has also called ‌for rallies on Saturday. Businesses in central Paris and other cities had already begun boarding up their windows and hiring private security in preparation for violence, French media reported.

The justice minister, Gérald Darmanin, said 174 of the 2,500 people arrested since last weekend’s rioting had been remanded in custody and more than 900 were being prosecuted. Two people have been arrested after Limoges town hall was set on fire.
sources.headline: Macron bans ‘illegitimate‘ protests in France as he tries to get a grip on unrest

sources.body:
El presidente francés, Emmanuel Macron, durante una reunión del Consejo de Seguridad en el Palacio del Elíseo, en París, este jueves. / TERESA SUAREZ / POOL / EFE

El presidente francés, Emmanuel Macron , busca poner coto a la nueva jornada de movilizaciones prevista para el próximo sábado y quiere vetar toda manifestación que no esté respaldada por organizaciones sindicales. Según anunció el mandatario tras una reunión con responsables de seguridad interior en el palacio del Elíseo con los servicios de inteligencia, los prefectos podrán prohibir las protestas convocadas por personas "que carecen de legitimidad para ello" . "Siempre que sea posible, las prohibiremos", prometió el presidente. Además, en el caso de las marchas de los sindicatos, las autoridades podrán modificar su recorrido "para proteger los centros de las ciudades, así como los comercios y edificios públicos", añadió. El objetivo del presidente es evitar que se repitan las escenas de caos de las manifestaciones del 17 de octubre .

"La recomendación general es que no haya manifestaciones en los próximos días (...), queremos que la calma vuelva a todas partes", añadió el jefe de Estado, antes de anunciar para este viernes la celebración de un Consejo de Defensa donde se adoptarán "medidas adicionales".

El Gobierno busca reducir la tensión política y las críticas tras los episodios de violencia registrados durante las protestas, mientras prepara el dispositivo de seguridad para la movilización prevista para el 24 de octubre. El ministro del Interior, Laurent Nuñez , presentará este jueves los detalles del operativo.

Mientras, el primer ministro, Sébastien Lecornu , tiene previsto recibir esta tarde en Matignon (sede del Gobierno) a representantes de los partidos políticos , en una reunión a la que asistirán Nuñez, el ministro de Justicia, Gérald Darmanin , responsables de los servicios de inteligencia y mandos de las fuerzas de seguridad. Lecornu ha prometido ofrecer información transparente sobre el desarrollo de las manifestaciones del 17 de octubre, incluidas las dificultades encontradas durante su gestión, con el objetivo de que todas las formaciones dispongan de los mismos datos.

Aunque se espera que todos los partidos invitados envíen representantes, varios han criticado la convocatoria y algunos de sus principales dirigentes no asistirán.

Es el caso del partido ultraderechista Agrupación Nacional (RN, en sus siglas en francés), que no estará representado por sus principales figuras, Marine Le Pen y Jordan Bardella . Y también de Horizontes, la formación del exprimer ministro y candidato al Elíseo, Édouard Philippe, y del Movimiento Demócrata de François Bayrou.

Lecornu también tiene previsto reunirse este jueves con los alcaldes de París , Lyon y Marsella , tres ciudades especialmente afectadas por los episodios violentos, en un intento de tranquilizar a las autoridades locales antes de las nuevas movilizaciones.

Las autoridades del país se mantienen vigilantes para este fin de semana ante las llamadas en redes sociales de volver a "tomar las calles" . Por ello, la prefectura de Lyon prohibió todas las manifestaciones para este sábado, y el presidente reiteró que los toques de queda establecidos en las principales ciudades se mantendrán hasta que la situación no esté estabilizada.
sources.headline: Macron prohíbe todas las manifestaciones que no estén organizadas por los sindicatos

stories.headline: Millions of websites face risk from two major PHP vulnerabilities

sources.body:
I once worked opposite a site where a shopping centre was being built.

We were warned there might be unexploded bombs from World War Two unearthed during the construction.

In the end, there were none, but procedures were put in place as a precaution and we all had to practice filing into designated safe zones inside our building.

The PHP story feels like the cyber equivalent of an unexploded bomb - I have never seen such a dramatic, public and global response to a cyber event that hasn't happened yet.

There has been no painful attack like the ransomware we saw knock out M&S and JLR in 2025.

But the potential threat is so serious that websites around the world have been taken down as a precaution.

Less than two months ago , 100 tech companies wrote an open letter warning the world to adopt a new level of cyber resilience in the age of AI.

It turns out we didn't have to wait very long to find out what they meant.

The weaknesses found in the PHP programming language, which is used by millions of websites, had been quietly resting there for years and are not easy to exploit.

One cyber security researcher told me he'd been up all night trying to do it as an experiment, but it was proving very difficult.

However, things that are very difficult for humans are increasingly very little trouble for AI.

The tech is getting a lot of credit here for assisting researchers in finding the bugs, and the PHP foundation, which oversees the programming language, was on the case and issued a fix.

It was supposed to be kept quiet until everyone had a chance to fix their sites - but the news was leaked.

From that point the clock started ticking.

As I write this, there are no reports that anyone or anything has succeeded in using the flaws to attack a site.

"There's a real dilemma," said Prof Alan Woodward from Surrey University.

"How do you alert people they need to be ready, and then that a patch is urgently required, whilst not alerting attackers?

"Basically you're telling everyone about the problem at the same time and hoping the defenders aren't awake enough to act as soon as the patch is out."

But we do know from large web companies like Cloudflare and Palo Alto Networks that millions of attempts have been made.

We probably won't know for a while whether it has worked for any criminals, because the companies affected might not be aware yet either.

As far as we know the unexploded bomb remains intact for now, and for some experts this is a success.

Gina Neff, Professor of Responsible AI at Queen Mary University, described this as a good news story.

"We've seen how a team of people supported by the large AI company have used AI to find the problem, work for months together to solve it and get everybody ready to be safe and secure," she told the Today Programme on BBC Radio 4.

"We have enormous capability to handle these risks."

But the baddies can use AI too, and those same tools are probably churning away right now trying to get in.

Cyber security authorities are warning website owners to fix the weaknesses immediately, but the patch only works on the latest version of PHP, so older sites will need to upgrade first.
sources.headline: Zoe Kleinman: PHP is the cyber equivalent of an unexploded bomb

sources.headline: En risc milions de webs del món per dues vulnerabilitats a PHP, un dels llenguatges més utilitzats

sources.body:
Las vulnerabilidades se descubrieron gracias a la IA

Creado a principios de la década de 1990, PHP es el lenguaje de programación que está detrás de aproximadamente el 70% de los sitios web en todo el mundo. Es también el lenguaje en el que se sustenta WordPress, el gestor de contenidos (CMS, por sus siglas en inglés), una de las plataformas más populares para blogs y webs personales, pero también las de pequeñas y medianas empresas. PHP es desarrollado y mantenido por la Fundación PHP, una entidad sin ánimo de lucro, que financia a investigadores e ingenieros para que contribuyan al mantenimiento, desarrollo y seguridad del lenguaje.

PHP, originalmente una abreviatura de Personal Home Page (Página de Inicio Personal) y posteriormente abreviada como PHP Hypertext Preprocessor (Preprocesador de Hipertexto PHP), se utiliza en el núcleo de plataformas populares de creación de sitios web como WordPress, pero también de Drupal —otro CMS— y PrestaShop o WooCommerce, un CMS y un plugin (propiedad de WordPress) muy populares para crear tiendas online.

Este miércoles por la mañana, muchos propietarios de estos sitios web recibieron un mensaje de sus proveedores de hosting advirtiendo que  se habían descubierto dos vulnerabilidades que afectaban precisamente a PHP. En ese mismo mensaje, los proveedores también avisaban de que se habían implementado medidas de mitigación, aunque dejaban muy claro que no eran la panacea y que, mientras no se instalaran los parches que PHP distribuyó ayer por la tarde, había riesgo de infección. Los parches hay que instalarlos en el servidor en el que está alojada la web y también PHP.

A diferencia de un sitio web estático, que siempre muestra la misma página a todos los visitantes, un sitio web PHP se considera dinámico: genera su contenido bajo demanda consultando una base de datos, verificando si el usuario ha iniciado sesión, mostrando información personalizada y actualizando el contenido en tiempo real. Es la columna vertebral de la World Wide Web .

PHP funciona con fragmentos de HTML intercalados. La página web hace una petición al servidor, un intérprete PHP ejecuta el código para, por ejemplo, consultar una base de datos y devuelve el resultado en HTML al servidor y este lo muestra en la página web. Según sea la consulta, PHP devuelve una respuesta u otra; por eso es dinámico.

Las vulnerabilidades descubiertas podrían permitir a los hackers infiltrarse en un gran número de estos sitios, desde tiendas en línea hasta servicios públicos. Por eso, muchas de ellas fueron desconectadas preventivamente mientras los desarrolladores trabajaban para proteger el código contra ataques.

¿Cómo descubrió la IA las vulnerabilidades?

Se usaron modelos de IA de vanguardia, como los de los gigantes estadounidenses OpenAI y Google, para descubrir debilidades en PHP en agosto. Este descubrimiento se mantuvo en secreto mientras se desarrollaba un parche.

En 2024, ya PHP fue sometido a su primera auditoría externa de seguridad “en años” y fue entonces cuando un desarrollador encontró los primeros indicios de un “problema” cuya resolución se retrasó por un “fallo estructural” en su proceso de decisión y sus recursos. “Para corregir el problema de agotamiento de memoria, el equipo de seguridad de PHP desarrolló varios enfoques alternativos”, pero “temía las repercusiones de publicar una solución equivocada” y tenía “numerosas responsabilidades”, lo que hizo que el trabajo en una solución “se estancara y se retomara repetidamente durante meses”, explicó entonces uno de los desarrolladores.
sources.headline: Qué es PHP y cómo se utiliza el lenguaje de programación que ha desatado la alarma

stories.headline: France reports the first known human Shamonda-virus case, saying there is no wider public-health risk

sources.body: France has reported the first-ever recorded case of a human contracting the Shamonda livestock virus, which is most commonly found in cattle. Public health authorities stressed that there did not appear to be any health risk to the public, adding that the infection had been "an exceptional case" involving a person with a severely compromised immune system.
sources.headline: France reports first human case of Shamonda virus, but says there's no public health risk

sources.body:
Investigations under way to determine whether virus normally found in livestock contributed to man’s death

A man in France has become the first human known to have contracted Shamonda virus, with investigations under way to explore whether it contributed to his death.

Shamonda virus is a type of bunyavirus and is spread by bites from infected midges. According to the Austrian Agency for Health and Food Safety , in animals such as cattle, sheep and goats it can cause diarrhoea, lack of appetite and a decline in milk yield, “as well as abortions and congenital abnormalities in newborn calves, lambs and kids”.

“In Switzerland and Germany, the presence of Shav [Shamonda virus] genetic material has also been reported in the brains of horses that died from neurological symptoms,” the agency said.

The virus has previously been found in farm animals outside Europe, but was first detected in livestock on the continent in the summer. The European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control (ECDC) said the patient in France was the first recognised human infection.

It also noted that he had already been seriously ill and had a compromised immune system, meaning it was unclear whether the virus played a role in his death this month.

“Investigations into whether the virus caused or contributed to the patient’s death and how the infection was acquired are ongoing,” the ECDC has said.

Prof Tom Solomon, the director of the pandemic institute at the University of Liverpool, said the risk to the general public appeared to be very low.

“Shamonda virus has been circulating in animals, particularly cattle, but also sheep, goats, horses and alpacas, for many years, yet this is the first recognised human infection,” he said.

“This suggests that transmission to humans is extremely unusual.”

But unknowns remain, he said: “We don’t know whether healthy people can become infected without developing symptoms, what symptoms the virus might normally cause, or how frequently it might cause serious disease.

“French authorities believe the neurological complications in this patient were very likely linked to the infection, although investigations are continuing.

“This is clearly concerning, but one exceptional case does not necessarily mean the virus poses a significant threat to the wider population.”

Dr Ben Brennan from the MRC-University of Glasgow’s centre for virus research, said there was currently no evidence of sustained transmission between humans.

“While this discovery warrants further scientific investigation and continued surveillance, it does not currently suggest a significant new public health threat to the UK,” he said.

“For most people, there is no reason to change their normal activities or take additional precautions.”
sources.headline: Shamonda virus detected in human for first time in France

sources.body:
The first known human case of the Shamonda virus (Shav) has been detected in a patient who died in early October, French authorities have said.

Health officials said it was an "exceptional case in a severely immunocompromised patient" and there was currently no risk to the public.

Shav is a disease that primarily affects cattle and can be spread by infected midges. Cases have also occurred in sheep, goats, alpacas and horses, but infections in people were previously unheard of.

The World Health Organization (WHO) and European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control (ECDC) said they were monitoring the situation, with French officials still investigating how the virus had spread to a human.

It is currently thought the patient contracted Shav through a midge bite in eastern France, the country's health and agriculture ministries said on Thursday, where cases were first identified in animals in the spring.

They said the patient was being treated for a serious illness in a Lyon hospital and experienced neurological complications thought to have been "very likely linked" to the virus, based on initial findings.

The statement stressed that their immune system was weakened, leaving them more vulnerable to getting ill.

"Until now, the Shamonda virus was considered non-transmissible to humans," it noted, having only been identified in animals "despite decades of circulation of the Shamonda virus in Africa and Asia".

Dairy herds that catch Shav from bites can experience fever, diarrhoea and poor milk production.

The WHO confirmed this was the first documented human case of the disease.

It said it had not yet made its own formal risk assessment, but advised that current information and knowledge of similar diseases suggested the case was isolated and "unlikely to lead to wider spread at this time".

"Transmissibility of midge-borne viruses also generally declines during the cooler months of the year," it added in a statement.

The ECDC said it was working with French and European partners to investigate the "potential public health implications" of the infection.

The first cases of the virus in Europe were identified in late July, the agency said. It has since been detected in farm animals in several countries, including Ireland, Germany, Italy and Spain, as well as in Jersey.
sources.headline: First human case of Shamonda virus detected in France, officials say

stories.headline: A fake polling firm may have distorted campaign narratives, fundraising and spending decisions in the US midterms

sources.body: A new company whose polls had influenced campaign decisions and helped shape the midterms narrative admitted that it was faking its polling data on Tuesday night, setting off a firestorm in the electionsphere. Wedgewood Polls, facing an imminent publication of an investigation from FiftyPlusOne showing it was fabricating its numbers, declared late Tuesday night that it had been an “experimental project” to show how an “entirely fabricated polling firm” could sway public opinion while painting themselves as the good guys. They’d left an impact and been included by multiple credible polling aggregators including The New York Times — and mentioned twice in POLITICO's Morning Score polling roundup. Speculation is flying about what, exactly, Wedgewood was trying to achieve, and there’s still little public information about the defunct company that had crowdfunded thousands of dollars for its fake data. Was it an effort to boost progressives Democrats in primaries? If so, were progressives or Republicans really behind it? Was it being used to game betting markets? Were top operatives using the bogus data to make spending decisions? Were aggregation accounts too quick to jump on posting the data? An email to the account listed on Wedgewood’s X account bounced back, and previous PDFs of polls that were tied to the account are no longer available online. Regardless of what Wedgewood said it was trying to achieve (they remain adamant the project “was never intended to sway an election or permanently mislead the public”) — pollsters, operatives and candidates alike said there were real world implications for posting fake data online. Mallory McMorrow, the unsuccessful Michigan Democratic Senate candidate who dropped out before her primary, said a fake Wedgewood poll that showed her crashing to single-digit support against Abdul El-Sayed and Rep. Haley Stevens “dried up” donations, “devastated” volunteers and led to numerous calls to exit the race. “It killed us,” McMorrow wrote on X . “These were some of the absolute worst days on the campaign. Especially for my team. There are no words to explain the morale blow, and nothing I could do or say to my team to fix it.” Jennifer Holdsworth, a Democratic operative who ran a super PAC supporting McMorrow, said the Wedgewood poll “was used by several donors to pull back funding at a time we were being outspent by $80 million.” The account also posted a poll showing democratic socialist Francesca Hong leading in the Wisconsin gubernatorial primary, when there was scant public polling, something that contributed to the narrative she was ahead before the election (which she lost). They also posted a poll showing the Mississippi Senate race within reach, just before Democrats plowed money into the state. Scott Colom, the Democrat running for the seat, blasted the poll to his press list as proof there was “massive momentum” behind him. That led election watchers to argue that Wedgewood’s data was being used to make spending decisions in top outside groups, which elicited a response from Democrats’ main Senate super PAC. “Absolutely not. We don’t make spending or strategic decisions based on external polling,” Lauren French, a spokesperson for Senate Majority PAC, said on X . In its investigation, FiftyPlusOne said it had included Wedgewood in its aggregator because the firm was founded by people who had worked in the polling industry previously. There’s also been broad finger-pointing at the aggregator X accounts that post polls frequently — and sometimes without verifying their accuracy. “You posted our polls multiple times. If you suspected it was fake, why did you post our results?” Wedgewood’s account shot back after Polling USA wrote that “my suspicions about Wedgewood were correct.” The whole ordeal illuminates just how big a problem polling could be in 2028, where both parties will have presidential primaries and polling can shift the narrative on a dime. “What I’m concerned about is essentially information pollution, things that are either intended to skew prediction markets or just straight misinformation flying around,” Charlotte Swasey, a pollster for the Democratic group Searchlight, told POLITICO Magazine recently. “It would be really difficult, especially in a primary, to tell people that what they’re seeing about their preferred candidate isn’t real.” A version of this article first appeared in POLITICO Pro’s Morning Score. On Tuesday, Oct. 20, FiftyPlusOne reached out to Wedgewood Polls, a self-professed polling firm, with a request for comment on an investigation we had conducted into their alleged survey research. They did not respond to our request, but instead posted a public statement on social media admitting that they had been fabricating data. They also reached out directly in social media DMs minutes before publishing their memo with an official comment: “Fuck you,” plus the name of an individual not affiliated with FiftyPlusOne.

Their statement alleges that FiftyPlusOne, the New York Times , and other poll aggregators did not conduct appropriate vetting of their firm prior to aggregating their polls; this is false. We reached out to them to ask who they were and confirm the methodology statement on their website. We were given two names, Jack Sims and Andrew Prater. We were able to independently confirm that Sims had previous experience in the polling industry and reviewed their methodology statement in detail. It is not atypical for a pollster to leave an existing firm, form their own, and self-fund some surveys to build reputation; we had no reason at the time to believe this case was any different. Wedgewood operated as if it were a legitimate polling firm, including collecting money from donors to conduct crowd-funded polls, and sharing raw survey data (which we now have confirmed was fraudulent) with FiftyPlusOne on Oct. 15, 2026.

stories.headline: Midterm candidates make affordability, the Iran war and data centres central issues in state-level debates

sources.body: With less than two weeks until Election Day, most statewide debates have come and gone. Democrats tried to paint their Republican opponents into corners over loyalty to President Donald Trump, and Republicans tried to stake out nuanced positions on the Iran war and data centers. Here’s what we learned from the more than two dozen statewide candidate debates that occurred — and from those that didn’t. Republicans walk a fine line with an unpopular Trump In debate after debate, Democrats tried to tie their opponents to the unpopular president. Republicans weren’t always willing to let them. Several candidates — especially in blue states — were willing to break with the president. In New Hampshire, GOP former Sen. John Sununu said he’s “never met President Trump” and emphasized he’s “never hesitated to stand up to my party or the president when they're wrong,” specifically criticizing Trump’s policies on trade, Iran and Ukraine. In Minnesota, Republican Senate nominee Michelle Tafoya said she disagreed with Trump’s tariff policy and immigration enforcement, and when asked if she would appear onstage with Trump, she demurred. “I am talking to Minnesotans. Theirs is the only endorsement that I care about,” she said. In Maine, GOP Sen. Susan Collins emphasized that she has voted against the president more than 100 times this year, and criticized his approach on Iran. Bobby Charles, the GOP nominee for governor and a former official in President George W. Bush’s State Department during the Iraq and Afghanistan wars, said he disagreed with Trump’s “extended engagement” in Iran because “I know what it means to get stuck in a place.” Some Republicans became frustrated by their opponents' efforts to tie them to the president. “He wants to make this about Donald Trump,” said former Rep. Mike Rogers (R-Mich.) “The bingo game ought to be, how many times can he put the word ‘Trump’ in any answer that he has given in the last, whatever, 30 minutes? It’s ridiculous.” But in some redder states, candidates were more willing to hug the president — recognizing support from his base will be critical to win . “We need the Trump voters to come out,” Sen. Roger Marshall (R-Kansas) said in a debate Wednesday. “Just like with my wife, I can disagree with her. Now, my wife is always right, and President Trump is not always right. But I do think that it's great that I have a relationship that I can pick up the phone and discuss with him the pros and cons of what he's contemplating.” It’s the economy, stupid Democrats hammered Republicans on affordability issues, blaming Trump’s tariff policy and Iran for spiking prices. In response, a few conceded some Trump policies were hurting them — while others tried to blame the last president. “That Bidenomics, that Green New Deal that my opponent voted for, that’s where all this inflation came from,” said Rep. Mike Collins (R-Ga.) in a Senate debate in early October. The other Collins, Susan, went the opposite way in blue-leaning Maine. “The bottom line is Troy and I both would have voted against the Canadian tariffs,” she said in an October 13 debate, after saying the Iran war was “not well thought out.” Rep. Ashley Hinson, the GOP nominee for Senate in Iowa, said she would pause the gasoline tax before acknowledging the effect of the war: "I trust in our U.S. military, the greatest fighting force in the world, to bring this to a close as quickly as possible, because I know people are being squeezed,” she said. Democrats largely sang the same tune on Trump’s policies. “These tariffs are crushing our state, and we'll repeal those tariffs,” said Sen. John Ossoff (D-Ga.). “The tariffs and the war in Iran has hurt Iowa more than any other state,” said state Rep. Josh Turek (D-Iowa). “If you appreciate having record diesel fuel prices … then I'd say vote for Roger Marshall,” said Adam Hamilton, the Democratic nominee running for Senate in Kansas. “If you want change, then I'd like to ask you to vote for me.” Everyone hates data centers Republicans and Democrats showed a remarkable similarity in their distaste for data centers even as their specific policy prescriptions diverged — a sign of the issue’s rapid ascent as a bipartisan bogeyman, even as Trump reiterates his support for them. Candidates from both parties called for local control. “Look, if you don't want a data center, I will stand up and defend it and make sure you don't get it,” said Rick Jackson, a Republican billionaire businessman running for Georgia governor. “Local communities know best,” said Hinson, the Iowa Republican. In Maine, both Senate candidates said guardrails should be installed to prevent the data centers from raising utility rates for local residents. In Iowa, both gubernatorial candidates — Democrat Rob Sand and Republican Zach Lahn — supported ending tax breaks for data center developers. In New Hampshire, both Senate candidates agreed with GOP Gov. Kelly Ayotte’s push for a statewide moratorium. “At the end of the day, it's up to our governor, our local leaders, to make decisions about any big infrastructure, transmission, power plants, new factories, and data centers should be treated just the same,” Sununu said. Gaffe gamechangers Debates can do candidates more harm than good, and some candidates had some cringey moments. In Alaska, Democratic former Rep. Mary Peltola appeared to be reading from a notecard throughout a recent debate, giving her opponent, GOP Sen. Dan Sullivan, a chance to pounce. "We weren't supposed to get these questions beforehand, were we?" he asked the moderator. “You can’t cue-card your way through the Senate,” Sullivan later wrote on social media. Sullivan had his own moment a few weeks earlier when he peeked at Peltola’s answer during a lightning-round question, prompting laughter from the audience. “Happy to help, Dan,” Peltola wrote on social media . In Kansas, Marshall faced loud chats of “you don’t live here” during a debate at the state fair, while speaking about his residence in Kansas and his home in Florida . In Maine, Jackson said Collins should “shut up” after a protester interrupted the debate and Collins claimed the demonstrator was “obviously one of Troy's supporters." "Oh, shut up,” Jackson said. “I don't even know that kid." Collins has pounced on the moment to try to paint Jackson as a sexist hothead; Jackson later said he did not regret his outburst. In Iowa, Hinson responded to a question about ensuring the solvency of Social Security by slamming young people’s saving habits . “We also need to be talking about millennials saving money,” she said. “Millennials are the worst group of savers in the country right now and have the least amount of savings.” The debates that didn’t happen Fear of gaffes may have cost voters a chance to see their candidates square off, as the longstanding political tradition of campaign debates took another hit this cycle. In Senate battlegrounds across the country, nominees in both parties outright refused to join their opponents onstage or carefully ducked debates. In Texas, Attorney General Ken Paxton rebuffed invitation after invitation (including one from Fox News), even after Trump urged him to get onstage. In Ohio, the Senate candidates still haven’t reached an agreement to debate. In North Carolina, there is no debate scheduled between the major-party Senate candidates for the first time in nearly 30 years . There doesn’t seem to be a partisan division over who will and won’t debate. Democratic Arizona Gov. Katie Hobbs and Ohio Democratic nominee Amy Acton refused to debate their opponents. So did GOP Gov. Greg Abbott of Texas and Sen. Tommy Tuberville of Alabama, who have rebuffed invitations to debate. “There’s so much difference between us, I mean, there’s no reason to get up there and argue about differences of opinion,” Tuberville, running for Alabama governor against Democratic former Sen. Doug Jones, told reporters in August. Andrew Howard, Jason Beeferman, Lisa Kashinsky, Aaron Pellish, Alec Hernandez, Erin Doherty and Jessica Piper contributed reporting.

El-Sayed in face-off against rival Rogers for Michigan Senate seat

Candidates in two key United States Senate races have faced off in their final debates, less than two weeks before the November 3 midterm elections .

In Michigan, Democrat Abdul El-Sayed and Republican Mike Rogers exchanged accusations on Wednesday regarding their political views and the US-Israel war on Iran.

In Kansas, Republican Senator Roger Marshall and his Democratic opponent, Adam Hamilton, disagreed about the rising price of diesel and President Donald Trump’s plan to import Russian fuel.

The results of both elections will influence which party ends up in control of the Senate. The Republicans currently dominate Congress’s upper chamber with 53 of its 100 seats. Democrats hold 45, and two senators are independents who caucus with the Democratic Party.

Here are some of the key takeaways from these debates:

Rogers questioned some of Trump’s tariffs, describing them as a “mixed bag”. While he supported taking steps to bring automobile manufacturing back to Michigan from China and Mexico, he questioned the impact of tariffs on Canada.

“I have stepped back and said maybe these Canadian tariffs were not well thought through,” Rogers said, referring to the close ties between the automobile industries of the two countries.

Michigan sits on the Canadian border and is the US state with the most car-manufacturing jobs.

Rogers insisted he would put Michigan’s interests first if elected.

“If it’s good for Michigan, I’m going to be for it. If it’s bad for Michigan, I’m going to be against it,” he said.

He pushed back against El-Sayed’s repeated references to Trump.

“The bingo game ought to be how many times can he put the word Trump in any answer that he has given in the last, whatever, 30 minutes,” he said. “It’s ridiculous.”

El-Sayed accused Rogers of supporting the war on Iran, which he blamed for rising fuel and food prices in the US.

He said he believed Iran had posed a threat to US national security but argued that the 2015 nuclear deal, negotiated under former President Barack Obama, had helped to contain it through diplomacy.

The Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action (JCPOA) was signed by Iran and several world powers, including the US. It placed restrictions on Iran’s nuclear programme, including strictly limiting uranium enrichment and compelling Iran to submit to international inspections, in exchange for sanctions relief.

Trump withdrew the US from the agreement in 2018, arguing that it failed to adequately address Iran’s nuclear ambitions and ballistic missile programme and support for armed groups in the region.

El-Sayed criticised Trump for abandoning the agreement during his first term and launching a war against Iran during his second.

El-Sayed argued that Americans have been left paying the price.

“The consequences of this war are that you are paying nearly $5 [per gallon, or 3.8 litres] in gas. You’re paying more in groceries because of the price of diesel,” he said.

stories.headline: Republicans' television-spending advantage is being diluted by Democrats' better ad rates and candidate fundraising

sources.body: Republicans are banking on a massive cash edge to help save their majority in Congress. But they are losing much of that advantage in an important arena: broadcast TV ads. Republicans have spent $677 million on those ads across 10 key Senate battleground states, compared to $479 million by the Democrats. But the GOP’s money isn’t going nearly as far because they’re more dependent on outside groups that pay much higher rates than candidates. The disparity has helped Democrats stay in the fight for Senate control amid an onslaught of GOP outside spending. In Ohio’s Senate race, Republican groups make up 63% of the $218 million spent. But in spite of their nearly 2-to-1 spending advantage over Democrats, they make up just over half of ads that are on the airwaves, according to data from the tracking service AdImpact. In Texas, Republicans have outspent Democrats by a 3-to-1 margin but have aired just 58% of the ads. And in Michigan, the GOP accounts for 60% of the spending but just over half of the ads. A large part of this discrepancy comes down to the mechanics of broadcast advertising. Candidates, and now political parties thanks to a recent Supreme Court ruling, are entitled to significantly lower rates. That has allowed Democratic candidates — who have posted bonkers fundraising hauls — to offset much of the GOP advantage in super PACs. Republican Senate candidates, on the other hand, struggled overall with their fundraising. And some GOP outside groups bought their ad time later, when it was even more expensive. “There are limitations to the impact of ‘big money’ in politics,” said Sean Cooksey, a Republican and former chair of the Federal Election Commission. “It's a good demonstration of the economics of campaign fundraising. Hard dollars really just go so much further.” The disparity also shows “the Republican overreliance on outside groups,” said Ian Russell, a Democratic admaker. “You get an eye-popping dollar amount, but it doesn't actually translate into as many spots as you would think relative to a well-financed candidate,” Russell said. “[Republicans] were just hoping that they could spend their way out of everything that was going wrong for them. But the problem is, their issues run much deeper than a few ad buys can fix. Especially when you've got monster fundraising hauls from the Democratic side.” Republicans in House and Senate races have long been more dependent on outside groups and megadonors, and for multiple cycles have seen their cash advantage undercut by fundraising strength from individual Democratic candidates. But that trend is particularly pronounced this year given the combination of Republican super PAC money and their candidates’ struggles. In 2024, Republican outside groups spent only about 15% more than Democrats on TV ads across House and Senate general election contests, according to a POLITICO analysis of AdImpact data. This cycle, GOP outside groups have spent 7% more. In a few states, the discrepancy between dollars and airtime is less stark. Republicans account for 60% of the spending in Maine’s Senate race and an equal percentage of the ads, according to AdImpact. That’s in part because Sen. Susan Collins has outraised her Democratic opponent Troy Jackson over the whole cycle, although Jackson, who didn’t launch his campaign until July, raised far more in the third quarter. The numbers show the shifting dynamics of campaign strategy after the Supreme Court opened the floodgates to more spending from parties by granting them the lower advertising rate. Republicans have been faster to take advantage of the new rules: Major coordinated spending efforts from the NRSC and RNC have helped their side significantly this cycle. Republicans have far outspent Democrats on Senate party-coordinated Senate advertising, $90 million to $34.6 million across TV, radio and digital ads, according to data from AdImpact. “If I were the leader of either party, I would say you shouldn't give a dollar, you shouldn't give a single penny to these super PACs until you've maxed out to the party committee,” Cooksey said. Some Republicans say that strategic errors have contributed to erasing their cash edge. A number of GOP strategists have also privately griped that MAGA Inc. — one of the major outside groups backing their candidates — bought TV airtime too late, forcing them to pay even higher rates and further draining resources and increasing the price of reaching voters. Republicans fretted for months about whether Trump’s well-financed super PAC, MAGA Inc., would get involved . The group has since spent heavily but only launched its first general election ad buys in September. “There is no question MAGA Inc. should have bought ads earlier in the cycle,” said one national GOP operative who was granted anonymity to discuss party strategy, noting that rates across the country increase as Election Day nears. Other top GOP outside groups, like the Senate Leadership Fund and the Congressional Leadership Fund, made their early advertising reservations much earlier in the cycle than MAGA Inc. Trump allies waved away that criticism. A person familiar with the Trump operation’s midterm planning, granted anonymity to discuss strategy, said it’s "indisputable that the spending from the Trump political effort has kept us competitive in many Senate races.” MAGA Inc. declined to comment. Still, GOP outside groups are utilizing their cash advantage in some underappreciated ways. Republican super PACs have massively outspent their Democratic counterparts on mail — roughly $157 million to $35 million for the general election — according to a POLITICO analysis of independent expenditure filings submitted to the Federal Election Commission. That’s led by a whopping $44 million in spending on mail across 24 races from the Trump-aligned No Going Back PAC, along with $23.8 million across 20 races from Elon Musk’s America PAC. GOP-aligned super PACs have also spent more than Democratic ones on phone calls and text messages, the data shows.
sources.headline: Why Republicans’ massive cash advantage is evaporating on the airwaves

El PSOE ha aceptado el debate entre los cuatro principales candidatos el 26 de noviembre en RTVE - Pedro Sánchez , Alberto Núñez Feijóo , Santiago Abascal y Ada Colau - y un debate cara a cara entre los dos principales aspirantes a presidente del Gobierno el 16 de noviembre en una televisión privada. Eso sí, la dirección socialista ha planteado como "indispensable que ambos encuentros se produzcan" .

En una nota pública, los socialistas afirman que no van a "consentir, bajo ningún concepto, el veto a la televisión pública", ya que el líder del PP, Alberto Núñez Feijóo ha dicho que no participará en ningún debate en RTVE. La misma nota resalta la "firme intención de participar en el mayor número de debates electorales" .

El Partido Socialista remarca que "no va a vetar a ninguna cadena privada", de igual forma que "no vamos a consentir, bajo ningún concepto, el veto a la televisión pública". Como argumentan en Ferraz, "la misión de servicio público que la Constitución y las leyes encomiendan a Radio Televisión Española tiene en los debates electorales una de sus expresiones más esenciales y garantistas".

Y recuerda el precedente de julio de 2023 . En las anteriores elecciones generales, recuerdan desde el PSOE, Pedro Sánchez acudió a los dos debates planteados , tanto al cara a cara organizado por Antena 3 como al debate a cuatro de RTVE. Sin embargo, Feijóo no acudió al de RTVE : "Plantó a la radiotelevisión pública en el debate a cuatro, hurtando a los españoles la posibilidad de contrastar su programa con el resto de fuerzas políticas".

Para 2026, el PSOE considera que al menos deben existir dos encuentros entre Sánchez y Feijóo siguiendo el esquema de 2023: un debate cara a cara organizado por un grupo privado y otro con los cuatro principales candidatos organizado por el ente público. "Siendo indispensable que ambos encuentros se produzcan", subrayan en Ferraz, dejando la puerta abierta a no asistir al cara a cara si Feijóo sigue rechazando el debate a cuatro en RTVE.

"En consecuencia", concluyen los socialistas, "el Partido Socialista acepta la invitación de RTVE para participar en el debate a cuatro el jueves 26 de noviembre y acepta participar también en un cara a cara organizado por medios privados el lunes 16 de noviembre .

Eso sí, el PSOE pide a todos los grupos mediáticos que cierren un acuerdo entre ellos para que la señal del debate se emita en abierto para todas las cadenas que lo quieran retransmitir, como ya ha anunciado que hará TVE.

sources.body: <p>No solo hay 10 horas de diferencia entre los dos vídeos. El primero, del PSOE, se publicó en la cuenta oficial de Pedro Sánchez a las 8.29 de la mañana de este miércoles, <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/elecciones-generales/2026-10-21/milei-saca-el-programa-de-la-motosierra-en-el-casino-ante-jaime-de-marichalar-ramon-tamames-y-figuras-del-pp-y-vox.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/elecciones-generales/2026-10-21/milei-saca-el-programa-de-la-motosierra-en-el-casino-ante-jaime-de-marichalar-ramon-tamames-y-figuras-del-pp-y-vox.html">justo antes de la ponencia de Javier Milei en el Casino de Madrid</a>. Y el segundo, del PP, pasadas las diez de la noche. Pero uno es real: grabado con cámaras, micrófonos y editado por un equipo de comunicadores audiovisuales. Y el otro, no: está generado por una aplicación de inteligencia artificial. Es más, es la primera vez que un partido político en España usa esta estrategia para suplantar la identidad y la voz de dirigentes y figuras políticas, como José Luis Rodríguez Zapatero, Begoña Gómez, la exportavoz socialista Montse Mínguez y hasta José Luis Ábalos, entre otros. En el caso de este último, quizá sea el más realista y parece que habla él mismo de verdad. sources.body:
“Sí, soy zurdo. Y a mucha honra”, advertía ayer Pedro Sánchez en un vídeo de precampaña que protagonizó con motivo de la polémica visita a España del presidente de Argentina, Javier Milei , en la que dedicó graves insultos al presidente del Gobierno como “impresentable dictador”, “liberticida” y “delincuente ladrón” entre otros improperios.

Si el jefe del Ejecutivo quiso exprimir con ese vídeo la visita del mandatario argentino, que podía incomodar al PP, los populares han contraatacado este jueves con otra campaña con un formato muy parecido pero hecho con inteligencia artificial (IA) y usando la imagen y la voz de líderes socialistas o del entorno del Gobierno admitiendo, en algunos casos, delitos, por los que han sido juzgados, se les juzgará o por los que se les investiga. El PP abre así un camino inédito que levanta no pocas dudas sobre su legitimidad e incluso legalidad.

La primera en aparecer en el vídeo, encabezado con el lema “Lerdos y orgullosos” en contraposición al hashtag #zurdosyorgullosos usado ayer, es Begoña Gómez, a quien se le hace decir: “Si tener una cátedra gracias a que mi marido es el presidente es de zurdos, pues sí, soy zurda”. La esposa de Pedro Sánchez está a la espera de juicio después de una controvertida instrucción del juez Juan Carlos Peinado.

“Si irse de p***s y cobrar comisiones ilegales es de zurdos, pues sí, soy zurdo”, dice un simulado exministro de Transportes José Luis Ábalos, condenado a 24 años de cárcel por el caso mascarillas.

El expresidente José Luis Rodríguez Zapatero aparece diciendo “si esconder joyas en una caja fuerte es de zurdos… pues sí, soy zurdo”. Esa circunstancia forma parte de la investigación que lleva a cabo el juez Calama sobre el rescate de la aerolínea Plus Ultra.

“Si contratar a unos matones para quitar de en medio a una jueza es de zurdos, pues sí, soy zurda”, señala una simulada Leire Díez, conocida como la fontanera del PSOE e investigada por el juez Santiago Pedraz por presuntos intentos de hacer descarrilar investigaciones al entorno del PSOE como la del hermano del presidente.

A la exportavoz del PSOE Montse Mínguez, el PP le hace decir “si usar la vivienda como arma política mientras oculto que mi novio tiene más de 30 pisos es de zurdos, pues sí, soy zurda”, aludiendo al motivo de su reciente dimisión. Y el último en aparecer es un simulado Santos Cerdán, ex secretario general del PSOE diciendo “si cobrar mordidas y pertenecer a una banda criminal es de zurdos, pues sí, soy zurdo”.

La portavoz del PSOE, Rebeca Torró, ha calificado el vídeo del PP en decalaraciones a La SER de “lamentable” y ha acusado a los populares de mantener una estrategia basada en la descalificación personal. “Llevan cuatro años de insultos y mentiras y ahora utilizan otro instrumento, que es la IA, porque no tienen otra cosa que el insulto permanente”, ha asegurado.

El formato replica el vídeo distribuido ayer por los socialistas en el que Sánchez decía que “hay quienes creen que nos insultan llamándonos “zurdos” o “zurdas”, aludiendo a la forma pretendidamente despectiva que Milei usa para referirse a los socialistas. Acto seguido el presidente señalaba las iniciativas que ha tomado su Gobierno en benefocio de la sociedad para poner en valor el hecho de ser zurdo, es decir socialista, lo que supone un motivo de orgullo y honra.

sources.body:
El aeropuerto de Roma Fiumicino el pasado verano 

Al final han sido Pedro Sánchez y Giorgia Meloni quienes han resuelto una crisis que llevaba casi tres meses enfrentando a España e Italia. Los gobiernos de ambos países han acordado no prorrogar los controles fronterizos que mantenían suspendida parcialmente la libre circulación dentro del espacio Schengen desde principios de agosto.

El anuncio ha llegado este jueves, después de una conversación telefónica entre los ministros del Interior, Fernando Grande-Marlaska y Matteo Piantedosi, que ha servido para concretar el acuerdo político alcanzado la semana pasada por los dos jefes de Gobierno en Bruselas.

Según el comunicado difundido por el Ministerio del Interior italiano, los dos ministros han mantenido una conversación “cordial”, programada después del encuentro entre Meloni y Sánchez al margen del Consejo Europeo. Tras analizar la situación, han decidido que las suspensiones de Schengen actualmente en vigor en ambos países no se prolongarán más. A cambio, Roma y Madrid reforzarán el intercambio de información para garantizar la seguridad del espacio europeo de libre circulación.

El acuerdo pone fin a un conflicto que desde el principio tuvo dos dimensiones. Por un lado, la técnica y de seguridad, gestionada por los ministerios del Interior, encargados de evaluar los riesgos derivados de la crisis migratoria de Ceuta y las posibles consecuencias para otros países europeos. Por otro, una dimensión política y diplomática, en la que los gobiernos de Roma y Madrid mantuvieron posiciones enfrentadas durante semanas. La decisión italiana de reintroducir los controles había provocado una dura reacción española y había convertido una medida excepcional prevista por Schengen en un motivo de enfrentamiento entre dos socios europeos.

El balance de estos casi tres meses de suspensión de Schengen ha sido, además, muy limitado. Los controles han permitido detectar a muy pocas personas en situación irregular y, según la información disponible, ninguna de ellas procedía de Ceuta, cuya crisis migratoria había sido precisamente el principal argumento utilizado por Roma para justificar las restricciones.

La salida llegó en el Consejo Europeo del 15 y 16 de octubre. Sánchez y Meloni hablaron personalmente y acordaron dar una semana a sus respectivos ministros para encontrar una fórmula que permitiera levantar los controles sin renunciar a la cooperación en materia de seguridad. Italia prorrogó entonces sus restricciones durante siete días, para hacer coincidir su vencimiento con el de las medidas españolas. Ahora, los dos ministros han confirmado que no habrá nuevas prórrogas.

Pero detrás del desbloqueo también hay un cálculo político. Según explicaron a La Vanguardia  fuentes próximas a Meloni, la primera ministra italiana no quería seguir dando lo que en su entorno consideran argumentos a Pedro Sánchez de cara a la campaña electoral española. La prolongación de una disputa bilateral podía terminar beneficiando políticamente al presidente socialista, una circunstancia que Roma prefería evitar.

stories.headline: Police find 74 migrants, including 10 children, overcrowded in a Ceuta apartment

sources.body:
Una operación de la Policía Nacional desarrollada el pasado martes ha permitido localizar a 74 migrantes en situación irregular hacinados y con lesiones de mordeduras de perros en un piso en el barrio del Príncipe de Ceuta, entre ellos diez menores, en una investigación que ha dejado un detenido que pretendía trasladar a estas personas a la península.

Según ha informado la Policía Nacional, la operación requirió un importante despliegue policial debido a la complejidad del lugar donde se encuentra el inmueble y se ha saldado con la detención de un ciudadano ceutí considerado el principal responsable de una organización criminal dedicada, presuntamente, al favorecimiento de la inmigración y otras actividades delictivas.

Durante el operativo los agentes han localizado a 54 hombres, 10 mujeres y 10 menores de edad no acompañados, lo que suma un total de 74 personas alojadas en el inmueble investigado. Al detenido se le imputan delitos de favorecimiento de la inmigración irregular, contra los derechos de los trabajadores, lesiones a menor y explotación laboral de menores.

Las pesquisas policiales han permitido obtener indicios de que algunos menores alojados en el inmueble podrían haber sido víctimas de agresiones físicas, incluyendo lesiones ocasionadas por mordeduras de un perro .

Asimismo, los agentes investigan la posible explotación laboral, tanto de menores como mayores de edad, que habrían sido utilizados para realizar diferentes tareas y trabajos, aprovechándose de su situación de necesidad y vulnerabilidad. "A las dificultades derivadas de la ubicación del inmueble se ha sumado la peligrosidad atribuida a la organización criminal, cuyos integrantes cuentan con numerosos antecedentes policiales", ha señalado la Policía en una nota de prensa.

El elevado número de personas localizadas durante la intervención se enmarca en un contexto de intensificación de la presión policial, que ha acabado con el desalojo de los asentamientos en la playa Benítez y El Trampolín, según la Policía. El desmantelamiento de los asentamientos ha propiciado el desplazamiento de una parte de los migrantes que permanecían en ellos hacia otros puntos de la ciudad, entre ellos el barrio de El Príncipe.

Ante esta situación, la Policía Nacional ha señalado que mantiene una "intensa actividad operativa", tanto en las inmediaciones como en la misma barriada. La operación ha supuesto, además, un importante golpe a la infraestructura logística del entramado criminal, que mantenía alojadas a numerosas personas en el inmueble a la espera de una oportunidad para facilitar su traslado irregular a la península.

La investigación se ha desarrollado gracias a la coordinación de las diferentes plantillas policiales repartidas tanto por la costa andaluza como a nivel central que están trabajando conjuntamente con la Fiscalía contra la lucha del tráfico ilícito de migrantes. Este jueves, el detenido ha sido puesto a disposición de la autoridad judicial.

stories.headline: The planned transfer of the R1 commuter-rail line is set to be signed next week

sources.body:
El govern espanyol assegura que continua avançant en el traspàs de Rodalies , i té previst aprovar el contracte programa de Renfe i completar la cessió de l'R1 "com més aviat millor". Ho ha afirmat el ministre de Transports, Óscar Puente , en una visita al president del govern, Salvador Illa, al Palau de la Generalitat.

Després d'una reunió d'una hora, el ministre i el president han comparegut per escenificar els avenços d'un traspàs que encara està pendent de la posada en marxa de l'empresa mixta de Rodalies , que hauria de començar a operar durant el 2027.

Puente ha declarat que les eleccions generals del 29 de novembre no aturaran el traspàs, tot i que ha reconegut que en poden "trastocar o afectar" alguns aspectes, com la cessió de l'R1. Així i tot, ha assegurat que la transferència d'aquesta línia és "irrevocable" i es farà efectiva "com més aviat millor". Tot i que no té data fixada, fonts del govern asseguren que la comissió bilateral Generalitat-Estat es reunirà abans de les eleccions.

Per demostrar els progressos, i en paral·lel al traspàs, Puente ha explicat que ja tenen llest el contracte programa amb Renfe, que determina els serveis que ha de prestar l'operadora i les seves obligacions econòmiques, d'uns 460 milions d'euros anuals.

El ministre ha especificat que aquest contracte, que seria fins al 2028, s'aprovarà al consell d'administració de Renfe , dimarts que ve. El mateix dia s'hi donarà llum verda al Consell Executiu del govern , segons ha afegit Illa.

En un context preelectoral, Puente ha reconegut que la situació de Rodalies està lluny de "l'excel·lència", però ha volgut traslladar un missatge "d'esperança" i ha assegurat que les inversions actuals serviran per millorar el servei de trens.

En aquest sentit, ha tret pit del fet que les incidències s'hagin reduït a la infraestructura ferroviària catalana en l'últim episodi de pluja. Si al gener, el pic de la crisi arran de l' accident de Gelida , en van registrar 630, aquest cop s'han reduït a 14.

Dins els compromisos anunciats, Puente també ha assegurat que els nous trens estaran llestos a principis del 2027 , una data que ha considerat "prudent". La previsió és incorporar-ne uns 112 o 113.

Pel que fa al traspàs integral de Rodalies, un dels grans compromisos d'investidura de Pedro Sánchez, falta saber si es podrà complir el calendari de posada en marxa de l'empresa mixta, prevista per al 2027. I si es continuarà avançant en la cessió de noves infraestructures, com l'R2 o l'R3.

L' acord per al traspàs es remunta al pacte d'ERC i el PSOE per a la investidura de Pedro Sánchez, el 2023. La cessió "integral" del servei i la infraestructura és una reivindicació històrica de la Generalitat.

Des de llavors, a banda del Pla de Rodalies per augmentar les inversions (amb 8.000 milions previstos), el govern espanyol i el català han avançat en la creació de l'empresa mixta. Es va formalitzar el gener del 2026 amb el nom de Rodalies de Catalunya i una participació del 50,1% de Renfe i el 49,9% del govern.

sources.body:
El traspàs de l’R1 de Rodalies, la línia que connecta Barcelona amb el Maresme i arriba fins a Maçanet-Massanes, afronta les últimes etapes després de gairebé dos anys de negociacions i tràmits administratius. El president de la Generalitat, Salvador Illa, i el ministre de Transports, Óscar Puente, aborden aquest dijous al Palau de la Generalitat l’estat del procés, que el Govern vol culminar entre finals d’octubre i principis de novembre. La proximitat de les eleccions espanyoles del 29 de novembre ha afegit pressió al calendari, davant la incertesa sobre la continuïtat dels compromisos ferroviaris si hi ha un canvi de govern a la Moncloa.

La convocatòria electoral converteix el traspàs de l’R1 en una de les carpetes que la Generalitat vol deixar resoltes abans dels comicis. El Govern confia que els acords es mantinguin independentment del resultat electoral, però un eventual canvi polític a l’Estat podria dificultar el desplegament de les transferències pendents, especialment pel que fa al finançament. Per això, la reunió entre Illa i Puente ha de servir per revisar els avenços i concretar els passos necessaris per tancar l’operació.

L’R1 és la primera línia escollida per iniciar el traspàs de la infraestructura ferroviària a Catalunya, en el marc dels compromisos polítics per avançar cap a una gestió pròpia de Rodalies. El procés va fer un primer pas formal el gener del 2025, quan el Govern va aprovar sol·licitar l’exclusió de la xarxa ferroviària d’interès general del tram comprès entre la bifurcació de la Sagrera i Maçanet-Massanes . Aquesta modificació és necessària per poder transferir-ne la titularitat a la Generalitat.

El procediment ha requerit inventariar els béns i les instal·lacions que s’han de traspassar, valorar-ne els actius i concretar les obligacions econòmiques associades . El calendari inicial s’ha anat allargant mentre les administracions preparaven les condicions de la transferència, i l’agost passat, la consellera de Territori, Sílvia Paneque, va situar a l’octubre la reunió bilateral necessària per aprovar-la. Aquesta setmana ha reiterat que els treballs del seu departament estan enllestits i que l’objectiu és tancar l’acord entre la setmana vinent i principis de novembre.

Per formalitzar-lo, cal convocar la Comissió Bilateral entre l’Estat i la Generalitat i la Comissió Mixta d’Afers Econòmics i Fiscals , que ha de concretar els aspectes financers. Posteriorment, l’acord haurà de rebre els avals institucionals corresponents. La proximitat del 29-N fa que el calendari sigui especialment rellevant: tancar el traspàs abans de les eleccions permetria deixar formalitzada aquesta primera transferència abans que els resultats puguin alterar les prioritats del govern espanyol.

stories.headline: Barcelona contains 32 of Spain's 100 most expensive rental areas, led by Pedralbes at an average €2,002 a month

sources.body: Barcelona concentra 32 dels 100 barris que més diners dediquen a pagar el lloguer de tot Espanya, segons les darreres dades de l’Institut Nacional d’Estadística (INE). La despesa mitjana destinada a pagar l’habitatge a la ciutat assoleix el seu màxim a Pedralbes, amb 2.002 € mensuals . És la segona zona més cara de tot l’Estat. Completen el podi barceloní les Tres Torres , amb una despesa mitjana de 1.911 € i la zona oest de Sant Gervasi – Galvany , que es queda a certa distància, als 1.744 €. L’últim barri barceloní que consta a la llista és Provençals del Poblenou , amb un lloguer mitjà de 976 €. Són les darreres dades disponibles, corresponen al 2024 , el mateix any que va entrar en vigor el topall del lloguer , que regula els preus dels arrendaments a les zones tensionades com Barcelona. Es tenen en compte, només, les ciutats de més de 250.000 habitants i estan fraccionades per zones, que no necessàriament coincideixen amb els barris oficials. Més de 1.000 euros de diferència Entre el primer barri barceloní que consta a la llista, Pedralbes, i l’últim, Provençals del Poblenou , hi ha més de 1.000 euros de diferència . Concretament, 1.026 €. Els salts de preus són més acusats a les posicions més altes de la llista. Per exemple, entre l’oest de Sant Gervasi – Galvany (1.744 €) i Diagonal Mar i el Front Marítim del Poblenou (1.508), per exemple, hi ha 236 € de diferència. També et pot interessar Quant costaria un lloguer a Barcelona si no hi hagués un topall als preus? Roger Torres i Liñán 1 minut de lectura En canvi, entre els barris que ocupen les darreres posicions, la diferència és molt més petita , d’entre 1 i 29 €. Si comparem l’est de la Sagrada Família (993 €) amb la zona que ocupa la posició següent, l’est de la Vila de Gràcia (992 €), el cost només varia d’1 €. I en aquesta mateixa línia, hi ha una diferència de preu semblant entre l’est de la Sagrada Família i el barri que té immediatament al damunt, la Salut (997 €). En aquest cas, són 4 €. Madrid, al costat de Barcelona A més de Barcelona, hi ha una altra ciutat que també predomina a la llista de l’INE: Madrid . La ciutat encapçala el rànquing: el barri de Recoletos és el més car d’Espanya amb un cost mitjà del lloguer de 2.037 € . Supera, per poc, els preus de Pedralbes. La capital espanyola ocupa 63 llocs a la llista. Entre les dues ciutats, acaparen 94 posicions . Només s’hi colen tres punts més del territori espanyol: un barri de Màlaga (posició 40), un altre de València (48) i quatre zones de Palma. sources.body:
Pagar el lloguer i les factures de la llum, l'aigua i el gas s'emporta, de mitjana, el 35,3% dels ingressos de les llars de Barcelona. Ho recull un informe de la Cambra de la Propietat Urbana de Barcelona que posa xifres al sobreesforç econòmic de les llars que viuen de lloguer.

El percentatge varia segons el districte, remarca la dificultat per accedir a l'habitatge i constata, un cop més, les desigualtats entre zones de la ciutat.

Mentre que a Ciutat Vella les despeses vinculades a l'habitatge representen, de mitjana, gairebé la meitat dels ingressos (47,4%), a Sarrià-Sant Gervasi es queden en el 26,6%.

En la majoria de districtes, se supera sempre la barrera del 30% dels ingressos de les llars. Aquest llindar del 30% és el que diverses institucions fixen com el límit d'esforç a partir del qual una llar pot tenir dificultats per afrontar altres despeses.

De fet, el Banc d'Espanya ja advertia en un informe del 2025 del sobreesforç de les llars per pagar el lloguer . En el cas de Barcelona, alertava que el 43,5% de les llars que viuen de lloguer superen aquest llindar recomanat.

En els últims anys altres estudis s'han fixat en aquesta sobrecàrrega del lloguer . A Catalunya, segons l'Observatori Metropolità de l'Habitatge de Barcelona (O-HB), el 25% de la població que viu de lloguer destina més del 40% dels ingressos a despeses de l'habitatge.

L'informe de la Cambra de la Propietat Urbana parteix de les últimes dades disponibles de la renda mitjana de les llars , del 2023. Els ingressos mitjans a Barcelona aquell any eren de 47.361 euros anuals .

Amb tot, l'estudi remarca que la renda mitjana no reflecteix exactament la situació de la majoria de les llars de la ciutat, ja que les rendes més altes fan pujar la mitjana. De fet, si es mira la mediana –un valor central sense tenir en compte el pes dels extrems–, la renda se situa en 38.979 euros anuals .

Per la seva banda, el preu mitjà del lloguer el 2023 es va situar en els 1.136 euros mensuals. Amb l'aplicació del topall de preus a partir del 2024, s'ha mantingut estable, tot i que en el període 2016-2025 ha pujat un 41,7%.

En el cas dels subministraments, l'informe té en compte una despesa anual de 3.086 euros a Catalunya el 2023, segons l'Enquesta de pressupostos familiars de l'INE, que no disgrega dades per ciutats.

Un any abans, coincidint amb el pic de la crisi energètica per la guerra a Ucraïna, la despesa era de 3.272 euros anuals. Però l'estudi apunta que si s'hagués tingut en compte aquesta xifra, l'esforç de les llars pujaria tan sols quatre dècimes fins al 35,7%.

Si les dades s'aterren als deu districtes de la ciutat, Ciutat Vella és on el lloguer i els subministraments s'emporten, de mitjana, més part dels ingressos d'una llar, gairebé la meitat, el 47,4%. El segueixen Sants-Montjuïc, Sant Martí i Nou Barris .

Cal remarcar, però, que l'estudi està fet a partir de la renda mitjana, la qual cosa vol dir que en un mateix districte hi pot haver llars on el lloguer i els subministraments s'emportin un percentatge encara més gran .

stories.headline: Barcelona's cruise industry opposes the planned increase in the stopover tourist tax to €30 by 2030

sources.body: Una cinquantena d’empreses del sector dels creuers han tornat a alçar la veu contra l’encariment de la taxa turística als creueristes d’escala , que el govern Collboni vol apujar fins als 30 € . Ara ho han fet amb l’elaboració d’un manifest en què deixen clar que rebutgen “aquesta imposició” perquè els discrimina , alhora que es mostren en contra “d’utilitzar la fiscalitat per reduir progressivament l’activitat de creuers a Barcelona”. Tot plegat ho han reivindicat des del moll de Drassanes, des d’on han llegit el manifest “a favor d’una Barcelona oberta al mar i al món “. En el text, les companyies també exigeixen diàleg a l’alcalde a l’hora de dibuixar el futur del sector, que coincideixen que ha de ser més equilibrat i “respectuós amb l’entorn”. “Som una part legítima del turisme de la ciutat, som professionals amb molts anys d’experiència i volem aportar el nostre gra de sorra a solucionar els problemes de la ciutat, però no volem ser els únics perjudicats “, ha demanat Irina Solomatina, de BC Cruise Service. Taxa als creuers d’escala: 30 € el 2030 El mes de setembre, el plenari va aprovar apujar la taxa als creuers d’escala progressivament, entre el 2027 i el 2030, fins arribar als 30 €. Ara mateix, un creuerista que està a Barcelona menys de 12 hores paga, en total, 11 € (6 € de taxa turística de la Generalitat + 5 € de recàrrec municipal). stories.headline: Barcelona's media-literacy platform calls for a permanent public strategy against disinformation

sources.body: La 3a Jornada de la Plataforma per a l’Educació Mediàtica (PEM), celebrada avui dijous a la Biblioteca Sarrià – J. V. Foix de Barcelona, ha reunit experts, periodistes i representants d’entitats per reflexionar sobre l’ impacte de la desinformació en la democràcia i els reptes que planteja la irrupció de la intel·ligència artificial. La sessió, emmarcada en la Setmana Mundial de l’Alfabetització Mediàtica i Informacional de la Unesco, ha estat inaugurada per la presidenta de la PEM i vicepresidenta del Consell de l’Audiovisual de Catalunya (CAC), Laura Pinyol, i pel gerent de Biblioteques de Barcelona, Ferran Burguillos. Durant la jornada, Laura Pinyol i el director de Relacions Institucionals de la Xarxa Audiovisual Local (XAL), Xavier Casinos, han presentat el Manifest per unes polítiques públiques estratègiques d’alfabetització mediàtica i informacional (AMI) a Catalunya . El document reclama al govern de la Generalitat que situï l’alfabetització mediàtica al centre de l’agenda política i impulsi una estratègia estable per combatre la desinformació i reforçar el pensament crític de la ciutadania. També et pot interessar Barcelona crearà una unitat per combatre les notícies falses a les xarxes socials Marta Casals Torres Roger Torres i Liñán 1 minut de lectura Educació mediàtica per a tots els públics La plataforma, integrada per una cinquantena d’entitats i institucions dels àmbits de l’educació i la comunicació, alerta de l’ augment de la desinformació i de la proliferació de continguts falsos a través de xarxes socials, plataformes digitals i serveis de missatgeria. Segons el manifest, aquesta situació posa en risc el dret de la ciutadania a rebre una informació veraç i contrastada. Una de les principals novetats de la proposta és que l’educació mediàtica no es limita als centres educatius , sinó que s’estén al conjunt de la població. El manifest defensa programes de formació per a infants, joves, persones adultes i gent gran , amb una atenció especial als col·lectius més vulnerables davant les bretxes digitals i informatives. També et pot interessar Polítics i xarxes: “Si no s’assessoren poden convertir-se en un mem i objecte de burla social” Andrea Cuerva Bonich 1 minut de lectura La desinformació afecta els processos electorals La conferència inaugural ha anat a càrrec de la investigadora del CIDOB Carme Colomina, que ha analitzat l’impacte dels algoritmes i de les plataformes digitals en l’accés a la informació. Colomina ha alertat que la desinformació i la polarització incideixen directament en la qualitat dels processos democràtics i electorals . La jornada s’ha completat amb dues taules rodones sobre la lluita contra la desinformació i la seva influència en el vot de la ciutadania, així com amb una exposició dedicada a l’alfabetització mediàtica i a l’ús responsable de les pantalles. Entre les entitats adherides al manifest hi ha betevé , que comparteix la demanda de la Plataforma per a l’Educació Mediàtica perquè l’alfabetització mediàtica i informacional esdevingui una prioritat de les polítiques públiques.
sources.headline: La Plataforma per a l’Educació Mediàtica reclama una estratègia pública contra la desinformació
